rachel (Marketing): Heads-up: I've pushed a new draft into the doc. Need a final hero headline, tightened benchmark language (no vagueness), gated webinar CTA, and HubSpot mapping. Target soft-publish Mon AM.
amit (Product): Taking a look. We should use med/p95 deltas and a short parenthetical about test conditions. No 'Xx faster' claims in hero.
claire (Growth): For CTAs: primary = 'Request a demo' (sales-qualified), secondary = 'Download benchmark kit' (gated). For first 48h traffic split 70/30 demo/kit.
eli (Design): Uploaded hero comps: device-frame and tiny-sparkline. Device-frame reads better on desktop; sparkline works in narrow widths. Suggest headline: 'Lower p95, dependable in production'.
rachel (Marketing): Draft headline options in the doc: A) 'Lower p95 at comparable quality' B) 'Predictable latency for production' — lean B for broader audience? Thoughts?
amit (Product): B is safer for non-eng buyers but we should include the med/p95 numbers in the subhead. I'll paste the appendix with exact figures and test harness: synth-load v3, 8xA100, seq1024.
claire (Growth): We'll gate the kit (3-slide summary + results.csv) behind webinar registration. CTA copy variants: 'Get the benchmark kit' vs 'Claim your benchmark kit'. I'll A/B test.
pete (Growth Ops): HubSpot plan: two lists -> "launch_demo" and "launch_benchmark"; utm_campaign=redwood-q2-launch; form embed I'll drop in the doc. Scoring: +40 for kit download, +60 for demo request, threshold 75 to SDR.achel (Marketing): Timeline recap: copy freeze 18:00 PT today, design freeze 18:30 PT, HS wired by 20:00 PT, staging preview 09:00 UTC Mon. Any final blockers?
eli (Design): Minor copy ask: subhead should call out 'real-world p95' not generic 'latency'. Updated mock.
claire (Growth): I'll prepare email copy for kit and demo confirmations and tracking tags.
build-bot: preview build queued for 2026-03-30T09:00:00Z for thread 1765439998
rachel (Marketing): Thanks team  once HubSpot code is in the doc I'll do a last editorial sweep and queue the preview.
